newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-SAMPRAS INTO SEMIFINAL AFTER FIVE-SET TUSSLE.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SAMPRAS INTO SEMIFINAL AFTER FIVE-SET TUSSLE.

text.p: World number one Pete Sampras fought his way into the semifinals of the Australian Open on Wednesday, winning a hard five-set tussle against Spanish challenger Albert Costa.
Sampras, the 1994 champion, beat Costa 6-3 6-7 6-1 3-6 6-2 to earn a semifinal tie with fifth seed Thomas Muster of Austria.
It was the second straight five-setter for Sampras, who narrowly survived against Slovakian teenager Dominik Hrbaty in Monday's fourth round.
Costa, one of three Spaniards who made it into the quarter-finals, ran down every ball and came up with seemingly impossible winners.
But the top seed kept his cool and powered through the final set, his serve leading the way.
Sampras sent down 23 aces in the match and won almost all his first-service points.
